title: MariaDB 13 Expands Oracle Compatibility and Improves Developer Experience and Observability
gist: MariaDB Community Server 13.0 reached general availability with deeper Oracle PL/SQL compatibility (REF CURSOR, RECORD types), a RETURNING clause for UPDATE, refined optimizer hints, and expanded observability, while MariaDB continues to treat rolling releases like 13.0 as fast-moving feature vehicles ahead of the next LTS, 13.3.

insights.claim: MariaDB 13 introduces native support for weak and strong REF CURSOR types and RECORD types in routine parameters and function return values, bringing MariaDB's cursor handling closer to Oracle PL/SQL to smooth the migration of Oracle PL/SQL-based enterprise applications.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Closer PL/SQL compatibility directly lowers migration cost for enterprises looking to move off Oracle, a recurring lever MariaDB uses to compete for Oracle's installed base.
insights.locator: To make the transition of Oracle PL/SQL-based enterprise applications smoother

insights.claim: REF CURSORs in MariaDB 13 can be opened, fetched, and closed, and used as local variables, package routine parameters, or package function return types, while RECORD support was expanded to stored routine parameters and stored function return types in addition to local variables, and RECORD can be combined with REF CURSORs to work with structured row data.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Enables more complex stored-procedure patterns previously exclusive to Oracle, removing a common blocker for porting stored-procedure-heavy applications.
insights.locator: Support for weak and strong REF CURSOR brings MariaDB's cursor handling

insights.claim: Neither REF CURSOR nor RECORD types are currently supported as a parameter or return type for non-package (global) routines in MariaDB 13.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: A concrete gap that migration teams evaluating MariaDB as an Oracle replacement need to account for before assuming full parity.
insights.locator: Neither REF CURSOR nor RECORD are currently supported as a parameter

themes.theme: Developer experience: DML and query optimizer improvements

insights.claim: MariaDB 13 lets UPDATE statements return the set of modified rows via the RETURNING clause, and combined with OLD_VALUE() this allows developers to retrieve both old and new values in a single database round trip; RETURNING was previously available only for INSERT and DELETE, and for UPDATE it is currently limited to single-table statements.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Cuts a common two-query pattern (read-before-update or read-after-update) down to one round trip, a direct latency and application-complexity win for developers.
insights.locator: MariaDB 13 also introduces a more straightforward way to work with data modified by UPDATE statements

insights.claim: MariaDB 13 builds on the optimizer hint framework introduced in MariaDB 12 by automatically assigning a query block name to Views, CTEs, and derived tables so hints can target them without explicit QB_NAME(), and adds QB_NAME locators to specify a path to deeply nested query blocks that cannot be targeted by name alone.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Makes query-plan tuning more practical on complex queries involving views and CTEs, reducing the manual boilerplate needed to apply optimizer hints.
insights.locator: Another area where MariaDB 13 brings improvements is query optimization

themes.theme: Observability and admin: programmatic metadata access

insights.claim: MariaDB 13 exposes init_rpl_role as a system variable so a server's replication role can be checked directly with SHOW VARIABLES or @@init_rpl_role, adds a CREATE_OPTIONS column to I_S.STATISTICS and I_S.COLUMNS to expose storage-engine-specific index and column options that were previously only available via SHOW CREATE TABLE, and adds columns to I_S.SYSTEM_VARIABLES indicating whether a system variable is deprecated.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Moves configuration and metadata inspection from parsing text output (SHOW CREATE TABLE) toward structured, queryable information_schema tables, easing automation and tooling built on top of MariaDB.
insights.locator: On the observability and administration front, MariaDB 13 makes server configuration

insights.claim: MariaDB positions itself as a rolling release aimed at getting the latest capabilities to users quickly rather than serving as the long-term stability (LTS) target, with the next planned LTS release being MariaDB 13.3.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Enterprises should treat MariaDB 13.0 as a feature-forward release to evaluate now but plan production stability commitments around 13.3, informing upgrade-timing decisions.
insights.locator: MariaDB is a rolling release aimed at getting the latest capabilities
